pages.text: "I am best at spinning this top." Gaga, who knew best, wound string around a wooden top. The classroom floor was wide and smooth. Gaga stretched their neck.
"Want to see a top spin to the end of the room?" Gaga flung it. Thud—it lay on its side. "Oh? Why will it not spin?"
Wind again, fling! Another thud. Three times, four times, it always fell over. Gaga's face flushed. "This top is broken."
Gaga dropped it in a box and turned away. Mio, who wanted to do everything alone, took that top, wound the string, and flung it. Whirr—it spun beautifully.
Gaga's neck drew back. "...It is not broken." Teacher Bau sat beside Gaga and picked up the top.
"Gaga, how far did you wind the string?" Gaga looked down at the half-wound string. "Wind it all the way, and keep holding the string until the end," Teacher Bau added.
Gaga wound the string all the way. Fling—the top fell over again. Still, Gaga picked it back up. "Falls over? Spin it again!"
A second try fell too. The third—whirr! The top spun for a long time in the middle of the room. "Spinning! I made it spin!" Gaga jumped.
Gaga told Mio, "One, string wound all the way! Two, hold on until the end! Three, if it falls, again!" They threw side by side. Two tops spun together on the floor.

Teacher Bau lifted Gaga high with both hands. "It was not broken; you just had not managed it yet." If it does not work, try another spin instead of blaming the top. Winding again, Gaga said, "Falls over? Spin it again!"
